markdown_report:
SASRec remains a feasible starting point; diagnoses favor testing recency and ranking discrimination before complex intent discovery. No improvement is established.

**Insights.** From the starting point: (1) causal attention combines recent and older interactions without explicitly suppressing stale interests. (2) shared embeddings support efficient scoring, but broad associations need not imply immediate usefulness. (3) average margins conceal difficult cases: Electronics has 14.95% sampled wrong ranks versus Movies_and_TV’s 3.03%; neither establishes validation HR@10.

From related work: (1) LSIDN and IDCLRec motivate persistent/dynamic separation without observing motivations. (2) HGN, HAM, TLSTSRec and DSASR establish substantial pooling/fusion precedent, reducing novelty. (3) gSASRec motivates multiple negatives; R²NS cautions against premature hard mining. (4) PCTM motivates strong recency/transition controls. Alignment scores near 0.54 do not establish collapse as the cause of errors.

**Framework.** Three complementary directions organize the search:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed minimal experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal representation | SASRec; HGN; LSIDN; TLSTSRec | Normalized convex recent/history fusion |
| Ranking discrimination | gSASRec; R²NS | Uniform multiple-negative objective |
| Directed association | Transition graphs; PCTM | Training-only transition-score blend |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a benefit and limitation.

- **Convex recent/history gate: 3/6/8/6/4.** Originality: diagnosis-driven adaptation / established fusion; potential: inexpensive foundation / incremental; user alignment: attenuates stale interests and emphasizes recent specifics / cannot establish compatibility; model alignment: may improve difficult distinctions / separation may fail elsewhere; difficulty: small branch / inference, normalization and controls require care.
- **Multiple-negative gBCE: 2/7/5/9/3.** Originality: established method / little novelty; potential: reusable objective / sampling sensitivity; user alignment: stronger discrimination / no temporal mechanism; model alignment: targets separation / margins may not generalize; difficulty: vectorized / memory cost.
- **Directed transition blend: 4/7/7/6/4.** Originality: useful adaptation / established counts; potential: complementary signal / sparse edges; user alignment: ordered associations / no verified complement labels; model alignment: alternative ranking evidence / popularity shortcuts; difficulty: sparse implementation / inference integration.

**Selected idea: normalized convex recent/history fusion.** At 0% progress, prioritize feasibility. Unlike additive fusion, convex fusion explicitly attenuates historical features, addressing stale influence and dilution of repeated recent preferences. Improving Electronics’ lower-tail separation remains a hypothesis.

Causally pool the latest five raw item embeddings, excluding padding; project and separately normalize both branches. Learn a scalar gate from their representations, cosine agreement and prefix length; initialize its final weights to zero and bias to −2. Fuse as `(1−a)h+a·r`, with identical output normalization/scoring across controls. Retain baseline loss and optimizer.

Use staged controls: baseline, popularity, last-item, recent-only, exponential pooling, fixed/scalar fusion, and parameter-matched SASRec/MLP; match selection effort and report per-category results. Bound this search prospectively within the shared budget. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10. Paired within-category user bootstrap intervals describe conditional uncertainty, not adaptive-selection bias. Sampled gains do not establish full-catalog gains. Compatibility, redundancy and actual intent remain unobserved.

idea.description: Replace the proposed additive recent-window residual with normalized convex fusion in each per-dataset SASRec model. A causal representation of the latest five raw item embeddings can explicitly reduce the contribution of historical features through a learned scalar gate.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale historical influence and dilution of specific recent preferences by broad associations. Convex fusion explicitly addresses both failure modes, whereas h + a*r leaves the historical coefficient fixed at one. Electronics’ 14.95% sampled wrong-rank rate and negative 10th-percentile margin motivate checking ranking separation, but do not establish that stale interests cause those errors. The method cannot infer verified compatibility, redundant ownership, or users’ actual motivations.
idea.implementation_notes: Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, original splits, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the effective SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200. Retain baseline loss, sampling, optimizer, batching and checkpoint protocol for the initial architectural comparison. At each valid position, average raw shared item embeddings over positions max(0,t-4) through t, excluding padding; never pool future items or targets. Project to the historical feature dimension and apply separate LayerNorm modules to historical and recent features. Use an explicit gate MLP: concatenate normalized h, normalized r, their cosine agreement, and log1p(cumulative nonpadding prefix length); apply Linear(2d+2,d), GELU, Linear(d,1), sigmoid. Initialize the final gate layer weights to zero and bias to -2, giving an initial recent weight of approximately 0.119. Compute z = LayerNorm((1-a)*h+a*r), then zero padded query outputs. Apply the same output normalization and shared-item dot-product scoring to fusion controls. Branch normalization reduces magnitude confounding; it does not prove that a gate measures intent. Pooling raw embeddings ensures locality; contextual states would retain older information. A trained historical encoder may adapt, so gate values alone do not establish stale-interest suppression. Preserve the literal baseline as a reference and include a history-only model with the same normalization when isolating fusion effects. Predeclare a bounded staged search: first compare baseline and window-five fusion; then prioritize last-item, recent-only and scalar/fixed-fusion controls before broader window, exponential-pooling and parameter-matched controls. Popularity-only and training-only transition baselines test shortcuts. Record exact configurations, checkpoint selection, candidate availability, GPU seconds and which controls were completed; do not claim superiority over unrun controls. Match objectives, sampling and tuning opportunities where applicable. Save architecture settings and weights beneath the trial directory; update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reconstructs the trained architecture with identical normalization, pooling, masking, scoring and dataset routing. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning measured metrics and definitions. view.model must reference the actual trained module; log2feats must return fused features and predict_score must match inference. Compute margins only at valid positions, using the same diagnostic sampling protocol across comparisons. Report gate summaries by observed history length as descriptive measurements, without interpreting them as motivations. Do not use unavailable categories, review ratings/text, item ratings/prices/stores, demographic attributes, or simulator traits. Empty category breakdowns cannot support category attribution. Use only public training histories and permitted titles, descriptions and timestamps; this initial variant needs histories only. Retain the native twenty training users, five per category, for full-catalog unseen-item qualitative recommendations; do not substitute sampled-candidate outputs. Select exclusively using host-computed, pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. If paired per-user hit indicators are exposed by the existing evaluator, bootstrap the same user indices within each category for both models, using 10,000 replicates and analysis seed 42; report percentile intervals for macro differences and category differences. Otherwise report available aggregate results without modifying the evaluator or inventing intervals. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. Bootstrap uncertainty is conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates and does not remove adaptive-selection bias or measure seed variation. Avoid interpreting sampled HR@10 as full-catalog HR@10. Keep execution single-GPU and charge all training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No experiment has been executed.
idea.pseudocode:
for dataset in FOUR_DATASETS:
    initialize per-dataset SASRec and fusion modules with training seed=42
    # Data preprocessing remains seed=0 and uses the original splits.
    initialize gate_final.weight = 0; gate_final.bias = -2
    for batch in unchanged_training_loader:
        _, sequence, positive, negative = batch
        valid = sequence != 0
        h_raw = sasrec.causal_features(sequence)
        e = shared_item_emb(sequence) * valid[..., None]
        # Prefix-sum differences implement trailing-window sums causally.
        sums = trailing_window_sum(e, window=5)
        counts = trailing_window_sum(valid, window=5)
        pooled = sums / clamp_min(counts[..., None], 1)
        h = history_layernorm(h_raw)
        r = recent_layernorm(recent_projection(pooled))
        length = cumulative_sum(valid)
        inputs = concat(h, r, cosine(h, r)[..., None], log1p(length)[..., None])
        a = sigmoid(gate_final(GELU(gate_hidden(inputs))))
        z = output_layernorm((1-a)*h + a*r)
        z = z * valid[..., None]
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(z, positive, negative)
        update_parameters(loss)
    save_weights_and_complete_architecture_config_under_trial_directory()
write_predictor_using_identical_features_scoring_and_dataset_routing()
# Execute the predeclared bounded comparison schedule within remaining GPU budget.
# Host independently computes pinned validation HR@10; retain per-category results.
# If existing evaluator exposes paired user hits, bootstrap paired differences.
# Keep final held-out evaluation independent; do not access test labels during search.

originality.positive: Combines a diagnosis-driven causal recent branch with an explicit mechanism for attenuating historical features under the matched benchmark.
originality.negative: Pooling, long/short interest fusion, complementary gates and normalized branches have substantial prior art; this is an incremental adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Creates a low-cost, interpretable experimental foundation for timestamp-aware fusion and later ranking-objective comparisons.
future_potential.negative: Its value depends on outperforming recency, popularity and parameter-matched controls; inferred recent preference does not establish practical intent.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses shared embeddings, causal window sums, normalization and a small MLP without requiring additional data or pretrained weights.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable causal masking, matched controls, generated predictor parity and diagnostic integration require more work than the architectural formula suggests.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal attention baseline and shared item scoring architecture.
limitations: Does not explicitly separate persistent preference from immediate intent.

related_work.title: LSIDN
contributions: Separates long-term preferences and short-term behavior through dedicated modeling and denoising.
limitations: Inferred interests do not establish actual user motivations.

related_work.title: IDCLRec
contributions: Models consistent interests and residual dynamic intent.
limitations: Its intent machinery is more complex than the proposed initial experiment.

related_work.title: TLSTSRec
contributions: Motivates adaptive fusion of temporal, long-term and short-term information.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this four-category benchmark or the proposed fusion.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates generalized BCE with multiple negatives to address sampled-BCE overconfidence.
limitations: Additional negatives increase computation and do not explicitly address stale preferences.

related_work.title: R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up and gradual stochastic hard-negative selection.
limitations: Hard negatives can include unobserved positives.

related_work.title: Do Sequential Recommendation Benchmarks Require Higher-Order Sequence Modelling?
contributions: Motivates a lightweight transition-count alternative using recency, smoothing and popularity adjustment.
limitations: Observed transitions do not establish complementary function or compatibility.
Reported full-catalog findings cannot be transferred directly to pinned sampled-candidate HR@10.

related_work.title: Hierarchical Gating Networks for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Combines feature and instance gates, pooled recent interactions, persistent preferences and item–item scores.
Establishes substantial prior art for pooling and gating, including Amazon evaluations and ablations.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed gate outperforms recency, popularity and parameter-matched controls under RecHarness.

related_work.title: HAM
contributions: Provides a simple pooled-association baseline evaluated against SASRec and HGN on Amazon data.
limitations: Its reported results do not establish effectiveness on this matched four-category protocol.

related_work.title: DSASR
contributions: Motivates drift-aware long/short modeling and reports learned-gate comparisons with fixed fusion.
limitations: Its demographic gate inputs are unavailable here.
Reported Amazon Beauty gains do not establish gains for this benchmark.

related_work.title: SLi-Rec implementation
contributions: Illustrates complementary sigmoid weights for long/short fusion.
limitations: Its target- and elapsed-time-conditioned gate differs from the proposed candidate-independent interaction-only gate.

related_work.title: AdaMCT
contributions: Provides adaptive local/global mixture ablations and normalization in both branches.
limitations: Does not establish a controlled advantage of the exact proposed convex formula over additive fusion.

related_work.title: SASRec PyTorch implementation
contributions: Illustrates embedding scaling and final LayerNorm, motivating explicit branch-scale controls.
limitations: An external implementation does not establish the exact normalization behavior of the pinned RecHarness baseline.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can change model ordering, including in expectation.
limitations: Does not invalidate the prescribed benchmark as the selection objective; it limits full-catalog interpretation.

related_work.title: On Sampling Top-K Recommendation Evaluation
contributions: Studies correspondence between sampled metrics and full-catalog metrics at mapped cutoffs.
limitations: Does not establish equivalence between sampled HR@10 and full-catalog HR@10.

related_work.title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
contributions: Provides paired-bootstrap methodology adaptable to paired user hit indicators.
limitations: User bootstrap intervals do not capture training-seed variation, candidate-resampling variation or adaptive model-selection bias.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how finite-sample model-selection variance creates optimistic selected performance.
limitations: Ordinary post-selection bootstrap intervals do not correct this bias; independent held-out evaluation remains necessary.
